name: Jamal
profile: Jamal is a 16-year-old in Transition Year who is highly capable academically but experiences significant anxiety around social situations, new environments, and unstructured time. He masks extensively at school, appearing to cope well, but experiences shutdowns at home. Jamal is interested in pursuing medicine but worries about work experience placements and interviews.
challenges: Severe social anxiety leading to avoidance of work experience opportunities
Masking at school resulting in exhaustion and home shutdowns
Difficulty with job interviews and professional social situations
Fear of new environments and unpredictable social demands
Lack of awareness among school staff about masking and autistic burnout
goals: Complete work experience placement with appropriate supports
Develop interview skills and professional communication strategies
Reduce need for masking through environmental accommodations

recommendedEBPs.title: Cognitive Behavioural Intervention
recommendedEBPs.rationale: Addresses anxiety thoughts and develops coping strategies for social situations

recommendedEBPs.title: Social Narratives
recommendedEBPs.rationale: Prepares Jamal for work experience and interview situations with clear expectations

recommendedEBPs.title: Video Modeling
recommendedEBPs.rationale: Demonstrates interview behaviours and workplace social interactions

recommendedEBPs.title: Self-Management
recommendedEBPs.rationale: Supports Jamal in monitoring stress levels and requesting accommodations

recommendedEBPs.title: Parent-Implemented Intervention
recommendedEBPs.rationale: Involves family in supporting Jamal's wellbeing and reducing masking pressure

recommendedEBPs.title: Virtual Reality
recommendedEBPs.rationale: Allows Jamal to practise interviews and explore work environments safely

implementation.cognitiveIntervention: School counsellor worked with Jamal on anxiety management, identifying unhelpful thoughts ('Everyone will think I'm weird') and developing realistic alternatives ('Some people will be understanding, and I can ask for what I need').
implementation.socialNarratives: Jamal and counsellor co-created narratives describing his work experience placement, what to expect, how to ask for breaks, and what to do if overwhelmed.
implementation.videoModeling: Jamal watched and analysed videos of medical professionals in workplace settings and mock job interviews, identifying helpful behaviours.
implementation.selfManagement: Jamal used a discrete anxiety scale (1-10) on his phone to monitor stress levels throughout the day and signal when he needed support.
implementation.parentIntervention: Family meeting with school discussed masking, autistic burnout, and home-school communication plan. Parents and school agreed on reduced homework during high-stress placement period.
implementation.virtualReality: Jamal used VR to virtually explore the hospital where his placement would occur and practised interview scenarios multiple times in a safe, controlled environment.

outcomes: Jamal completed 2-week work experience placement in local hospital with accommodations (quiet break space, clear schedule, designated staff contact)
Successfully navigated interview process for college open day medical programme, disclosing autism and requesting accommodations
School implemented 'masking awareness' training for all TY teachers
Jamal reports feeling 'less alone' and more confident requesting supports
Home shutdowns reduced from 4 per week to 1 per week during placement period
reflections: This case highlighted how masking can make autistic students 'invisible' to support systems. Jamal appeared to be coping until family raised concerns. The VR component was transformative - Jamal practised interview scenarios 15 times before his real interview, which he said made it feel 'almost routine'. Collaboration with parents was essential; school initially thought Jamal was 'doing fine' because he wasn't displaying obvious distress. The placement succeeded because the hospital was briefed in advance and provided specific accommodations. Staff training on masking and burnout was valuable for identifying other students who might need support.

context.duration: 20 weeks preparation, 2 weeks placement, ongoing support
context.supportLevel: Tier 2 - counsellor support, family liaison, and workplace accommodations
